rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so this candidate escalates aggressiveness: SecurityGain and DiversityGain are raised across the board (SUB to 0.85 as the cheapest high-value pass; FLA and BCF to 0.80/0.75 to add control-flow flattening and bogus-edge density on the five display-style functions, which are the largest at 241-441 bytes and thus can absorb a dispatcher and opaque predicates). SPLIT's DiversityGain is boosted to 0.75 because splitting basic blocks in these small C++ methods creates more blocks for FLA/BCF to scramble, amplifying synergy at near-zero cost. Cost penalties stay moderate rather than low — RuntimeCost 0.50-0.55 on BCF/FLA reflects that this is a small benchmark where main is only 300 bytes, so excessive flattening overhead is the main remaining risk; CorrectnessRisk on FLA/ICALL (0.30) is kept elevated because C++ member functions with this-pointer arithmetic and indirect dispatch are the likeliest ICE/miscompile sites, and preserving the round-1 correctness result is the constraint that gates further escalation.
